title.$t: Aging Health Medical Glossary (Offline Test Feed)

summary.$t: Abnormally low magnesium levels in the blood (typically below 1.7 mg/dL), which can contribute to muscle cramps, fatigue, irregular heart rhythms, and impaired vitamin D activation in older adults.

content.$t: Abnormally low magnesium levels in the blood (typically below 1.7 mg/dL), which can contribute to muscle cramps, fatigue, irregular heart rhythms, and impaired vitamin D activation in older adults.

summary.$t: Progressive, age-related loss of skeletal muscle mass, strength, and physical function that increases the risk of falls, frailty, and metabolic decline—especially during rapid weight loss.

content.$t: Progressive, age-related loss of skeletal muscle mass, strength, and physical function that increases the risk of falls, frailty, and metabolic decline—especially during rapid weight loss.

summary.$t: The proportion of a nutrient, supplement, or medication that is absorbed through the digestive tract and enters systemic circulation in an active form usable by the body.

summary.$t: The reduced, electron-rich active antioxidant form of Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) that supports mitochondrial ATP energy production and becomes harder for the body to convert from ubiquinone after age 50.

summary.$t: A subclinical state in which intracellular and bone magnesium stores are depleted even though standard serum magnesium blood tests still read inside the normal reference range.
